text.KJV NEH 12:7: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the chief of the priests and of their brethren in the days of Jeshua.
text.BHSA NEH 12:8: וְהַלְוִיִּ֗ם יֵשׁ֧וּעַ בִּנּ֛וּי קַדְמִיאֵ֥ל שֵׁרֵבְיָ֖ה יְהוּדָ֣ה מַתַּנְיָ֑ה עַֽל־הֻיְּדֹ֖ות ה֥וּא וְאֶחָֽיו׃
text.KJV NEH 12:8: Moreover the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, which was over the thanksgiving, he and his brethren.

A.name: Jeshua
A.line: Levite whose sons (descendants) returned to Judah after captivity (EZR 2:40)
A.notes: of the sons of Hodaviah.  A peer/brother of Kadmiel? (EZR 2:40). Father of Jozabad (EZR 8:33)
family: descendant-of hodaviah-5 (Hodaviah, his sons (descendants) returned to Judah after captivity (EZ)

B.name: Jeshua
B.line: explained the law to the people (NEH 8:7), stood on the Levites platform (NEH 9:4), and exhorted Israel to bless the Lord (NEH 9:5)
B.notes: "of" Kadmiel (NEH 7:43), son of Kadmiel (NEH 12:24). Father of Joiakim (NEH 12:10)
family: son-of kadmiel-2 (Kadmiel, stood on the Levites platform (NEH 9:4) and exhorted Israel )
son-of kadmiel (Kadmiel, his sons (descendants) returned to Judah after captivity (EZ)
descendant-of levi (Levi, third-born son of Jacob (GEN 29:34), son of Leah)

why: The Hebrew names Jeshua alongside Binnui and Kadmiel among the Levites, following the priests identified with 'the days of Jeshua' (12:7), which best fits A's return-era setting. B's law-reading activities and identification as a son of Kadmiel fit a later setting, although this verse supplies no patronymic to make the distinction certain.
